current_tip: 'Préparer' (to prepare) follows the standard -er pattern. The stem 'prépar-' stays the same for all forms.
fixed_tip: 'Adorer' = to love/adore. Stronger than 'aimer'. With general nouns, use the article: 'adorent le chocolat'.

current_tip: 'Aider' (to help) is a regular -er verb. When followed by a verb, use 'à': aider quelqu'un à faire quelque chose.
fixed_tip: 'Détester' = to hate. With abstract nouns, French requires the article: 'il déteste le bruit' (he hates noise).

current_tip: 'Acheter' gets an accent grave in stressed forms: j'achète, tu achètes, il achète. The 'nous' and 'vous' forms keep no accent: achetons.
fixed_tip: 'Nous' form of -er verbs: drop -er, add -ons. 'Préparons le petit déjeuner' = we prepare breakfast.

current_tip: 'Passer' has many meanings: to spend (time), to pass, to take (an exam). Context determines the meaning.
fixed_tip: 'Porter' means both 'to carry' and 'to wear': context determines. 'Portent des lunettes' = they wear glasses.

current_tip: 'Gagner' means both 'to win' and 'to earn'. Context tells you which: gagner un match (win), gagner de l'argent (earn).
fixed_tip: 'Inviter' is regular -er. 'Des amis' uses partitive 'des' = some. French requires this where English omits 'some'.

current_tip: 'Rentrer' means to come/go back home. It implies returning to a familiar place, unlike 'retourner' which is more general.
fixed_tip: 'Obéir à' = to obey. Regular -ir verb with -iss- in plural. Requires 'à': 'il obéit à ses parents'.

current_tip: 'Arriver' means 'to arrive' but can also mean 'to happen': il m'arrive de... (it happens that I...).
fixed_tip: 'Entrer dans' = to enter. Requires 'dans': 'vous entrez dans le magasin'. Uses 'être' in passé composé.

current_tip: 'Tomber' (to fall) uses 'être' as its auxiliary in the passé composé: je suis tombé, not *j'ai tombé.
fixed_tip: 'Garer' = to park. 'Garer la voiture' = to park the car. Reflexive 'se garer' = to park/find parking.

current_tip: 'Porter' means both 'to carry' and 'to wear'. Context makes it clear: porter un sac (carry) vs porter une robe (wear).
fixed_tip: 'Toucher' = to touch. Regular -er verb. 'Le mur' = the wall.

current_tip: 'Envoyer' is irregular in the future: j'enverrai (not *j'envoierai). One of the few -er verbs with an irregular future stem.
fixed_tip: 'Partager' = to share/split. Keeps 'e' before -ons: 'nous partageons'. 'L'addition' = the bill.

current_tip: 'Devoir' expresses obligation: 'je dois partir' = I must leave. It also means 'to owe'.
fixed_tip: 'Pouvoir' + infinitive = can/able to. 'Tu peux venir?' = Can you come? Informal question via intonation.

current_tip: 'Appeler' doubles the 'l' in stressed forms: j'appelle, tu appelles. But nous appelons keeps single 'l'.
fixed_tip: 'Remplir' = to fill out. Regular -ir with -iss-: 'nous remplissons'. Same pattern as 'finir'.

current_tip: 'Montrer' (to show) takes a direct object. 'Montrer quelque chose à quelqu'un' = to show something to someone.
fixed_tip: 'Nager' = to swim. Like 'partager', keeps 'e' before -ons: 'nous nageons'. 'Dans la piscine' = in the pool.

current_tip: 'Laisser' + infinitive means 'to let someone do something': laisse-moi parler = let me speak.
fixed_tip: 'Réfléchir à' = to think about. Regular -ir with -iss-. Requires 'à': 'je réfléchis à la question'.

current_tip: 'Poser une question' = to ask a question. French 'poses' the question rather than 'asking' it.
fixed_tip: 'Bavarder' = to chat. Regular -er. 'Au café' = at the café ('au' = à+le contraction).

current_tip: 'Présenter' is used reflexively to introduce oneself: 'je me présente' = I introduce myself.
'Avoir besoin de' = to need. French 'has need of' something rather than 'needing' it directly.
fixed_tip: 'Aller à' = to go to. 'Au' = à+le: 'vous allez au marché' = you go to the market.

current_tip: 'Savoir' = to know facts/how to. 'Connaître' = to know/be familiar with people or places.
fixed_tip: 'Vouloir' + infinitive = to want to. Irregular: je veux, tu veux, il veut, nous voulons, vous voulez, ils veulent.

current_tip: 'Puis-je' is the inverted form of 'je peux' (formal). Use 'puis-je' instead of 'peux-je' in questions.
fixed_tip: 'Bienvenue dans' = welcome to. 'Notre' = our (invariable). 'Nouveau' before masculine noun = new.

current_tip: 'Qui' = Who. 'Qui est-ce ?' = Who is it? 'Qui est-ce qui' = Who (as subject). 'Qui est-ce que' = Who/whom (as object).
fixed_tip: 'D'accord' = OK/agreed. Common in conversation. 'Disponible' = available.

current_tip: 'Avoir peur de' = to be afraid of. French 'has fear of' something.
fixed_tip: 'Croire' = to believe. Irregular: je crois, tu crois, il croit, nous croyons, ils croient.

current_tip: 'Donner' takes a direct object (the thing) and an indirect object with 'à' (the person): donner un cadeau à quelqu'un.
fixed_tip: 'Rendre' = to return/give back. Regular -re: je rends, tu rends, il rend. 'À la bibliothèque' = to the library.

current_tip: 'Penser à' means to think about something/someone. 'Penser de' means to have an opinion about.
fixed_tip: 'Coller' = to glue/stick. Regular -er. 'Dans l'album' = in the album.

current_tip: 'Comment' (how) is used for manner: 'comment ça marche ?' = how does it work?
fixed_tip: 'Excusez-moi' (formal) / 'excuse-moi' (informal). Hyphen links verb and pronoun in imperative.

current_tip: 'Aller' + infinitive forms the near future: 'je vais manger' = I'm going to eat. Very common in speech.
fixed_tip: 'Faire' = to do/make. Irregular: je fais, il fait, nous faisons, ils font. Used in many fixed expressions.

current_tip: 'Avoir' + age in French: 'j'ai vingt ans' (I have twenty years), not *je suis vingt ans.
fixed_tip: 'Mettre' = to put/set. Irregular: je mets, tu mets, il met. 'Mettre la table' = to set the table.

current_tip: 'Avoir envie de' = to feel like/want. More casual than 'vouloir'.
fixed_tip: 'Conduire' = to drive. Irregular: je conduis, tu conduis, il conduit. 'Trop vite' = too fast.

current_tip: 'Faire attention' = to be careful/pay attention. French 'makes attention' rather than 'paying' it.
fixed_tip: 'Sortir' = to go out/leave. Irregular -ir: je sors, il sort. 'Du' = de+le: 'sort du bureau' = leaves the office.

current_tip: 'À quelle heure' = at what time. Always use 'à' before 'quelle heure'.
fixed_tip: 'Avoir' in inversion: 'avez-vous des enfants?' Formal question form. 'Des' = some (partitive).

current_tip: 'Avoir l'air' + adjective = to look/seem: 'tu as l'air fatigué'. The adjective usually agrees with the subject.
fixed_tip: 'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.

current_tip: 'Qui' (who) as subject doesn't need 'est-ce que': 'Qui parle ?' is already a complete question.
fixed_tip: 'Arriver' uses 'être' in passé composé: 'je suis arrivé(e)'. 'En retard' = late. Regular -er in present.

current_tip: 'Venir' is an irregular -ir verb: je viens, tu viens, il vient. Note the -ien- stem change.
fixed_tip: 'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.

current_tip: 'Intéresser' also works backwards like plaire: 'ce sujet m'intéresse' = this subject interests me.

fixed_tip: 'Aller à' = to go to. 'Au' = à+le: 'vous allez au marché' = you go to the market.

current_tip: 'Plaire' in passé composé: 'ça m'a plu' (past participle 'plu'). Don't confuse with 'plu' from 'pleuvoir' (rain).

current_tip: 'Falloir' (il faut) is impersonal – only used with 'il'. It expresses necessity: 'il me faut' = I need.

fixed_tip: 'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.

current_tip: 'À bientôt' = see you soon. Other options: 'à demain' (see you tomorrow), 'à plus tard' (see you later).

fixed_tip: Three question forms: intonation ('Tu viens?'), 'est-ce que', or inversion ('Viens-tu?').

current_tip: With 'être' verbs, plus-que-parfait agrees: 'elle était partie' (she had left). Agreement like passé composé.
fixed_tip: The futur simple (will): infinitive + endings (-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont). Some verbs have irregular stems.

current_tip: 'Tu vois' / 'tu sais' = you see/you know. Common fillers in informal speech.
'Avoir la chair de poule' = 'to have goosebumps'. Literal: 'hen skin'.
'Il pleut des cordes' = 'it's pouring'. Literal: 'it's raining ropes'.
fixed_tip: 'Des' = some (partitive plural). French requires it where English uses no article: 'des enfants' = children.

current_tip: 'Faire' in passé simple: je fis, il fit, nous fîmes, ils firent.
'Ce n'est que...que': restrictive structure 'only...'.
fixed_tip: 'Être' (to be): je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont.

current_tip: Inversion after direct speech: 'dit-il', 'répondit-elle'. Standard in French narratives.
fixed_tip: The imparfait describes ongoing, habitual, or background past actions. Formed from the 'nous' present stem + -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.

current_tip: 'Venir' in passé simple: je vins, il vint, nous vînmes, ils vinrent. Very irregular.

fixed_tip: Reflexive verbs use 'se' + verb: 'se laver' (to wash oneself). The pronoun changes: je me, tu te, il se, nous nous, vous vous.
